methodology.timing: Process wall in measurements; library wall excluding TPC-H pool initialization in library_measurements. Library timing includes table/session/job creation, worker startup/join, generation and batch consumption.
methodology.cpu_and_rss: Whole fresh process, including setup. Ordered Populate consumers run on the calling thread; reference partitions consume/drop on their workers. Reference comparisons therefore include delivery-semantics differences; before/after comparisons keep the ordered API.
methodology.output: Full Arrow RecordBatches are generated and consumed; no IPC encoding, file output, disk flushing or cache drops.
methodology.scale: SF0.1, SF1 and SF100 sweep; SF10 controls and targeted experiments. DSB rejects fractional scale factors.
methodology.batch_defaults: Populate TPC-H/SSB 8192, TPC-DS/DSB 2048; Rust reference 8000. No batch/chunk overrides.
methodology.reference: Rust tpchgen/tpchgen-arrow and tpcdsgen/tpcdsgen-arrow 4.0.0. Reference tables use up to the requested number of source partitions, including small TPC-DS tables.
methodology.aggregate: Selected tables follow TableName::ALL unless explicitly listed. The multi-thread reference adapter pops table/partition jobs from a shared Vec in LIFO order. Populate schedules remaining work per source and fuses compatible TPC-DS sales/returns. Aggregate speedups include scheduling and fusion differences; aggregate times cannot be obtained by adding isolated table times.
methodology.controls: stream consumes/drops each batch on its worker; TPC-DS stream is unfused. Do not attribute an ordered-fused versus stream-unfused difference solely to buffering.
methodology.sampling: One excluded warmup plus seven fresh-process samples, with three for single-thread controls. Three-engine sweeps rotate/reverse order; the initial two-engine SSB/DSB sweep has main first. All follow-up experiments strictly alternate baseline/candidate. Timing runs are sequential and exclude builds, profiles and tests.
methodology.timestamps: Initial scale-sweep timestamps were captured on completion; started_at is reconstructed from process_wall_s and original completion retained.

This report covers the pinned earlier implementation, with final SSB refinement at 3d7c2572; post-rewrite integration and profiles are recorded separately. Experimental binaries are identified by SHA and source patch.

specification.profile_interpretation: Whole-process user-cycle samples include setup and repeated generation. Flame widths are CPU samples, not elapsed time or predicted speedup. perf stat is a separate run; inspect multiplex percentages.

findings.scope: Generation-only Arrow, matched mimalloc, 32 ARM cores. No claim about IPC/TBL/Parquet writing or SSD throughput.

profile_findings.assembly: Comments use scalar indexed loads into a 300 MiB pool. Short comments call memcpy. PRNG and fanout work remain dominant; scheduler is not a major CPU leaf.
Pricing contains four runtime signed divisions and serial RNG arithmetic. Forced inlining removes the separate pricing symbol but regresses measured time.
Annotated hot instructions occur in surrogate-key selection and quantity/null loops. A local key-range bound did not improve the overall generator.

experiments.name: Forced pricing inlining
experiments.lesson: Fewer calls/divisions do not establish a win. Large fused callers can lose from code shape and register pressure; the precise mechanism is not isolated.

experiments.name: Bound inventory key preparation to remaining rows
experiments.lesson: Less source-level work was insufficient. No reliable aggregate gain at SF1/SF10; SF100 inventory worsened.

experiments.name: Grow all generic chunks to about 32 jobs per worker
experiments.lesson: Regular SSB lineorder benefits, wide flattened rows and TPC-H do not. Narrow the adjustment to regular SSB lineorder.

complex_opportunities.area: TPC-H batched comment-prefix loads and prefetch
complex_opportunities.evidence: 26.56% of lineitem SF100 CPU samples in comment-view construction; scalar random indexed loads in assembly.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Process multiple independent offsets at once and test software prefetch distances.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: Medium; architecture-sensitive memory latency/cache tradeoff, inline versus long views, safe bounds and fallback paths.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Full output equality, SF1/10/100, single/multithread, multiple allocators and at least a second CPU architecture.
complex_opportunities.speedup: Unmeasured; CPU share is not a wall-time gain.

complex_opportunities.area: TPC-H vectorized RNG and column generation
complex_opportunities.evidence: 45.56% row construction, 11.58% Lehmer fill and 9.09% integer-column groups at SF100.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Batch independent RNG streams and fuse selected intermediate column passes with fanout construction.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: High; preserve exact per-order skip distances, variable child counts, every unused reference draw and chunk-boundary behavior.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Stream-equivalence tests, arbitrary source ranges/chunks, all full table hashes, portable fallback.

complex_opportunities.area: TPC-DS batched pricing/RNG with fixed column builders
complex_opportunities.evidence: 14.06% aggregate pricing CPU, 48.69% fused channel CPU; the latter includes more than builder overhead.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Generate a block of prices/keys and fill typed column slices with one reserve/validity check per block.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: High; variable sales/returns fanout, exact decimal truncation, per-column RNG budgets, null masks and potential unsafe initialization. Forced inlining alone was slower.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Reference equivalence for all channels, returns-only/fused cases, custom batch sizes and cancellation/error safety.

complex_opportunities.area: Bounded ordered-delivery window and reusable workers/buffers
complex_opportunities.evidence: Current scheduler drains out-of-order work into an unbounded BTreeMap; small-scale times include thread lifecycle and cross-thread destruction.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Bound outstanding chunks per source, persist worker pools, recycle buffers only when ownership permits.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: High; preserve caller-thread ordered callbacks, borrowed closures, arbitrary retained Arrow batches, error cancellation and deadlock-free progress.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Slow-first-chunk and slow-consumer tests, retained batches, cancellation/panics, memory bounds and small/large scale performance.
complex_opportunities.speedup: Unmeasured; primary benefit may be predictable memory rather than throughput.

complex_opportunities.evidence: Earlier blanket channel splitting regressed aggregate 887 to 1031 ms.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Separate immutable distribution/permutation setup from each mutable seeded row generator, or use reusable worker-local generators.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: High; vendored upstream interfaces, exact seed positioning and independent chunks; mutable state must never leak across tasks.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Full before/after equality and reference checks across all channels/scales; retain the known native-C item mismatch caveat.

complex_opportunities.evidence: Surrogate-key branches are hot within inventory, but inventory is only 2.53% of aggregate SF100 CPU and the local range shortcut failed.
complex_opportunities.possible_change: Build surrogate keys once per week/session and share immutable arrays across chunks.
complex_opportunities.difficulty: Medium to high; cache size, scale/session identity, initialization contention and lifecycle may outweigh saved work.
complex_opportunities.proof_required: Week/warehouse boundaries, nonzero ranges, multiple simultaneous sessions, cache memory and aggregate timings.

findings.interpretation: None of these is impossible. The difficulty is preserving exact generation and API semantics while proving a net improvement across scales. This campaign keeps only measured, limited changes.

pricing_inline_assembly.interpretation: The store-channel body grew from 14032 to 14964 bytes and static [sp]-relative memory instruction sites from 326 to 367. These are code-shape observations, not dynamic spill counts or a proven causal attribution of the slowdown.

binary_derivation.scaled-cap-mimalloc: 1a89e1d1 plus pricing-inline.patch and the generic chunk-growth implementation from rejected-global-and-inventory.patch; inventory change absent
